body.rationale: IPS status: ratified, as stated in the brief; I treat the limits as binding. I ranked for what the CIO can build from, favouring compliance and covariance-based methods over return-forecast methods, per the late-cycle finding in section 4.3. (1) cvar_minimization is IPS-clean with the best backtest of the compliant set (Sharpe 0.74, drawdown -18.7%). Its reviewer confirmed it ran as designed. The weaknesses are real: only about 2.9 effective assets, and volatility tuned to exactly 8.00%. Both are fixable by blending with broader sleeves. (2) tail_risk_parity is built on downside co-movement and reads no return forecast. Its only breach is volatility (7.67% against the 8% floor), which is marginal. Its drawdown is -20.9% and its effective N is 14.4. The reviews found only framing errors, such as the 14.4-of-18 denominator. (3) resampled_efficient_frontier is compliant and well diversified (effective N 13.1). The reviews flag that its -24.84% drawdown sits only 16bp inside the limit, so it ranks below the two above. (4) inverse_volatility is compliant, broad (effective N 14.8) and has no tuned parameter. It ignores correlation, and about 43% sits in credit and sovereign sleeves that fall together, so it is a stable base, not a lead. (5) black_litterman is compliant, with a -21.9% drawdown and an ex-ante Sharpe of 0.42. Its reviewer found the equilibrium prior distorted because overlapping ETF AUMs are double-counted. It also relies on return views, which is what the regime argues against. My first choice beats my fifth on tail-risk evidence. cvar_minimization has a shallower drawdown (-18.7% against -21.9%) and a higher backtest Sharpe (0.74 against 0.68), and it does not depend on a contaminated prior or on return forecasts. I flag market_cap_weight. It has a -40.6% backtest drawdown, a CRO risk score of 0.80 and a breach of the drawdown limit. Reviewers also showed its ETF-AUM weights are not a true market portfolio, since they double-count overlapping US style funds. I did not rank or flag adversarial_diversifier. Its value is orthogonality, which should be kept in the ensemble, and its three IPS breaches keep it out of my top five.
